stories.title: Critical FortiMail Zero-Day Flaw Exploited in Attacks Allows Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Writes
stories.abstract: Fortinet has released security updates for FortiMail to address critical path traversal vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-104286, which is currently being exploited in the wild. CISA has added this flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to the risk of arbitrary file writes.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated remote attackers to write arbitrary files, potentially leading to full system compromise of email security appliances.
stories.action: Update FortiMail to version 8.0.2, 7.6.7, or 7.4.9 immediately.

stories.title: Apple CoreGraphics PoC Emerges as WhatsApp PDF Checks Hint at Possible Delivery Path
stories.abstract: A public proof-of-concept has emerged for CVE-2026-86950, a critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Apple's CoreGraphics engine. Attackers are actively exploiting this flaw via malicious PDF files containing crafted fonts to target specific individuals on iOS and macOS devices.
stories.why: This zero-day is actively exploited in the wild, posing a significant risk for targeted surveillance and remote code execution on Apple platforms.
stories.action: Update all iOS and macOS devices to the latest available security versions immediately.

stories.title: Armatura LLC Armatura One
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in Armatura One access control software allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code, access databases, or seize control of physical security systems. These flaws include hard-coded credentials, cryptographic keys, and insecure deserialization.
stories.why: Exploitation grants full administrative control over physical access systems, posing a severe risk to critical infrastructure and facility security.
stories.action: Update Armatura One to version 4.7.2 or Armatura One (USA) to 4.6.1 immediately.

stories.title: Cisco Warns of Attackers Exploiting Critical Authentication Bypass in SD-WAN Manager
stories.abstract: Cisco has patched a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain administrative access via the API. CISA has confirmed active exploitation and added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: This vulnerability grants full administrative control over network management infrastructure, making it a high-priority target for remote attackers.
stories.action: Update Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88772 Exploit Details Show Pre-Auth Path to Shellcode Execution
stories.abstract: Citrix has released patches for multiple vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and Gateway, including two flaws currently under active exploitation. These critical issues, notably a memory overflow in the DTLS protocol, allow for unauthorized access and potential system compromise.
stories.why: Edge devices are high-value targets for initial access; active exploitation of these vulnerabilities poses a significant risk of network compromise.
stories.action: Update NetScaler ADC and Gateway to the latest versions specified in the Citrix security bulletin.

stories.title: Johnson Controls EasyIO Neo Series EC and CW Controllers
stories.abstract: Johnson Controls released patches for EasyIO FG, Neo, and FS32 controllers to address vulnerabilities involving sensitive information exposure and cleartext data transmission. These flaws could allow unauthorized actors to intercept credentials and session data, potentially facilitating further attacks against critical infrastructure systems.
stories.why: Exploitation of these vulnerabilities in industrial control systems could lead to unauthorized access and compromise of critical facility operations.
stories.action: Update EasyIO FG, Neo, and FS32 firmware to the latest versions provided by Johnson Controls.

stories.title: 'Warlock' ransomware used in attacks on critical infrastructure in Portuguese, Spanish-speaking countries
stories.abstract: A China-linked threat actor dubbed Warlock is actively targeting critical infrastructure across Portugal and Spanish-speaking nations. The group has been leveraging various Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities since July 2025, exhibiting a hybrid operational style that blends cybercriminal tactics with state-sponsored espionage techniques.
stories.why: The group's focus on critical infrastructure and exploitation of SharePoint vulnerabilities poses a significant risk to enterprise and government network integrity.
stories.action: Audit and patch all Microsoft SharePoint instances to the latest available security versions.

stories.title: Police Arrest 16-Year-Old Suspected of Running KillSec, Seize Ransomware Leak Site and Servers
stories.abstract: International law enforcement dismantled the KillSec ransomware operation, seizing servers and a leak site containing 110 terabytes of exfiltrated data. Authorities arrested three individuals, including a 16-year-old suspected of acting as the group's primary administrator.
stories.why: The disruption of a significant data extortion site highlights ongoing law enforcement efforts to dismantle ransomware infrastructure and identify key threat actors.

stories.title: Dell CSM Flaws Enable Unauthenticated Admin Access and Root on Kubernetes Nodes
stories.abstract: Dell patched critical vulnerabilities in its Container Storage Modules for Kubernetes. The most severe flaw, CVE-2026-63688, involves a missing authentication check in the gRPC server, potentially allowing unauthenticated attackers to gain administrative control and root access to underlying nodes.
stories.why: These flaws permit full system compromise of Kubernetes infrastructure, bypassing storage authorization controls and granting attackers elevated privileges over the cluster.
stories.action: Update Dell Container Storage Modules to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit Zimbra Flaw to Deploy Web Shells and Harvest Authentication Secrets
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical command injection vulnerability in Zimbra Collaboration Suite, tracked as CVE-2026-73570. By leveraging the Simple Network Management Protocol, attackers can achieve remote code execution to install web shells and exfiltrate sensitive mailbox credentials.
stories.why: This flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution, providing attackers a direct path to compromise internal email infrastructure and harvest organizational data.
stories.action: Patch Zimbra Collaboration Suite immediately to mitigate CVE-2026-73570.

stories.title: Fortinet sounds the alarm over actively exploited FortiMail zero-day
stories.abstract: Fortinet has disclosed a critical zero-day vulnerability in its FortiMail secure email gateway. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code. Exploitation is currently occurring in the wild, and some versions remain without an available security update.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote code execution on email infrastructure provides attackers with a high-value entry point for lateral movement and data exfiltration.
stories.action: Check Fortinet's advisory for patch availability and restrict management interface access immediately.

stories.title: Kiteworks & Citrix Incidents Show Challenges of Zero-Day Response
stories.abstract: Recent security incidents involving Kiteworks and Citrix highlight significant inconsistencies in how vendors manage zero-day disclosures. Organizations faced varying levels of transparency, ranging from emergency shutdown instructions to delayed communications regarding active exploitation of vulnerabilities.
stories.why: Inconsistent vendor disclosure practices complicate incident response and risk assessment for security teams relying on third-party software.

stories.title: [Control Systems] Moxa security advisory (AV26-995)
stories.abstract: Moxa has disclosed multiple vulnerabilities affecting its MGate 3000 and 5000 series protocol gateways. Administrators should investigate these security flaws, which include issues identified by CVE-2026-86325 and CVE-2026-86326, to determine the impact on their industrial control environments.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in industrial gateways can provide attackers with unauthorized access or control over critical operational technology networks.
stories.action: Review Moxa security advisory AV26-995 and apply available firmware updates for affected MGate devices.

stories.title: Antino Backdoor Uses Outlook and OneDrive for C2 in China-Nexus Espionage Campaign
stories.abstract: A China-linked threat actor is targeting government and policy entities across Asia with a novel backdoor called Antino. The malware leverages Microsoft Outlook and OneDrive infrastructure to facilitate command-and-control communications, enabling long-term espionage against organizations in countries including India, Taiwan, and the Philippines.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates sophisticated abuse of legitimate cloud services for stealthy data exfiltration and persistent remote access in sensitive geopolitical sectors.

stories.title: Microsoft’s X account hacked in crypto pump-and-dump scheme
stories.abstract: Unauthorized actors gained control of Microsoft's primary X account to broadcast fraudulent cryptocurrency promotions. The attackers leveraged the company's massive follower base to push a pump-and-dump scheme involving a Clippy-themed token before the account was recovered.
stories.why: High-profile account takeovers demonstrate that even major tech entities remain vulnerable to social engineering or platform-level security failures.

stories.title: Attackers Abuse ChatGPT Custom GPTs to Deliver RAT via ClickFix Lures
stories.abstract: Attackers are weaponizing custom GPTs to masquerade as legitimate software, tricking users into visiting malicious websites. These sites employ ClickFix social engineering tactics to deceive victims into executing malware, effectively turning trusted AI platforms into vectors for trojan delivery.
stories.why: This demonstrates how threat actors exploit the inherent trust users place in established AI ecosystems to bypass traditional security awareness.

stories.title: ThreatsDay: AI-Powered Zero-Day Chain, 543K Live Secrets, Model Inspection RCE and 13 More Stories
stories.abstract: Recent security findings highlight how routine system operations like caching, model inspection, and data storage can be weaponized. Attackers are increasingly exploiting these standard functions to execute code or access sensitive information, proving that mundane features often harbor significant, overlooked vulnerabilities.
stories.why: Standard system features are being repurposed as attack vectors, requiring security teams to re-evaluate the risk profile of common, trusted operational processes.

stories.title: Bitget Confirms Third-Party Zero-Day Behind $387.5 Million Cryptocurrency Theft
stories.abstract: Cryptocurrency exchange Bitget reported that a zero-day vulnerability within a third-party security tool facilitated a massive theft of $387.5 million. Forensic analysis by SlowMist confirmed the attackers utilized a bespoke exploit to compromise the platform's defenses.
stories.why: This incident highlights the significant supply chain risk posed by third-party security software, which can serve as a backdoor into high-value infrastructure.

stories.title: macOS Users Targeted by Fake Zoom Installer Carrying CloudSyncD Backdoor
stories.abstract: Attackers are distributing a malicious Zoom installer for macOS that deploys a two-stage backdoor known as CloudSyncD. The malware uses a fake installation process to harvest user credentials and establish persistent unauthorized access to compromised systems.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates sophisticated social engineering targeting common productivity software to gain elevated privileges and persistent control over macOS environments.

stories.title: ABB Protection and Control IED Manager PCM600
stories.abstract: ABB's PCM600 software contains two vulnerabilities involving improper path restrictions and incorrect permission assignments. These flaws allow local attackers to escalate privileges or overwrite sensitive system files by exploiting the Scheduler Service, which operates with elevated LocalSystem account permissions.
stories.why: Exploitation could grant unauthorized users full control over industrial control system management software, posing significant risks to energy sector infrastructure.
stories.action: Update ABB PCM600 to a version beyond 2.14.

stories.title: Monta monta.app
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in the Monta charging management platform expose infrastructure to unauthorized administrative access and denial-of-service attacks. The flaws include improper authentication, session management failures, and credential protection issues affecting all versions of the application.
stories.why: These flaws allow remote attackers to seize control of critical energy and transportation infrastructure, potentially disrupting charging services globally.

stories.title: Podcast: The FBI Was Hacked. We’ve Seen the Data
stories.abstract: Journalists at 404 Media have obtained and verified data allegedly stolen from the FBI. The report suggests a significant security breach occurred within the agency, though specific details regarding the scope and method of the intrusion remain limited.
stories.why: A successful compromise of federal law enforcement infrastructure indicates potential systemic vulnerabilities and risks to sensitive investigative data.

stories.title: OpenAI Parts Ways With Three Safety Researchers Over Sensitive Information Mishandling
stories.abstract: OpenAI terminated three safety researchers following an internal probe that concluded they improperly accessed and distributed confidential company data. The organization stated these actions violated established internal security protocols regarding the handling of sensitive information.
stories.why: Internal data leakage by personnel with high-level access highlights significant insider threat risks and potential gaps in organizational data governance.

stories.title: Hackers stole Pentagon personnel records of over 3 million people
stories.abstract: The Department of Defense confirmed that attackers compromised the Defense Manpower Data Center, resulting in the theft of personal records belonging to over three million current and former military personnel. The breach occurred within the agency's human resources management system during late 2025.
stories.why: This represents a massive exfiltration of sensitive government personnel data, likely providing adversaries with significant intelligence for targeting or social engineering campaigns.

stories.title: Mississippi mayor says ransomware incident led city to shut down systems
stories.abstract: Vicksburg, Mississippi, suspended municipal digital operations following a ransomware attack. Local officials are currently collaborating with the FBI to investigate the breach and restore affected government services.
stories.why: Municipalities remain high-value targets for ransomware actors, often resulting in prolonged service outages and potential exposure of sensitive constituent data.

stories.title: Meari IoT Cloud Platform OpenAPI Service
stories.abstract: The Meari IoT Cloud Platform OpenAPI Service contains critical authorization flaws across all versions. These vulnerabilities permit authenticated attackers to modify device settings, execute unauthorized actions, and exfiltrate sensitive data, including network information, owner details, and device credentials.
stories.why: Unauthorized access to IoT management platforms can lead to widespread device compromise, data theft, and potential pivot points into internal networks.

stories.title: Police Target KillSec Ransomware Group with Arrests and Seizures
stories.abstract: Law enforcement agencies have dismantled the KillSec ransomware operation, successfully apprehending multiple primary suspects associated with the group's criminal activities.
stories.why: Disrupting active ransomware syndicates reduces the immediate threat landscape and provides intelligence on current extortion tactics.

stories.title: Kiteworks security advisory (AV26-988)
stories.abstract: Kiteworks has released security updates for its Core, Email Protection Gateway, and Secure Data Forms products. Versions prior to 9.5.0 and 9.5.1 are impacted by vulnerabilities, necessitating an immediate review of the vendor's advisory for remediation steps.
stories.why: Unpatched file transfer and email security gateways are high-value targets for data exfiltration and unauthorized network access.
stories.action: Update Kiteworks Core, EPG, and SDF to version 9.5.1 or later.

stories.title: Fortra security advisory (AV26-987)
stories.abstract: Fortra has disclosed multiple critical vulnerabilities affecting various versions of its Core Privileged Access Manager and BoKS Manager software. The flaws include heap buffer overflows, stack buffer overflows, and out-of-bounds read vulnerabilities within key components like boks_sshd and boks_portmux.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities could allow unauthenticated attackers to trigger memory corruption, potentially leading to remote code execution or unauthorized system access.
stories.action: Review Fortra security advisories and update BoKS Manager and Core Privileged Access Manager to the latest versions.

stories.title: Google security advisory (AV26-984)
stories.abstract: Google has released security updates for the Chrome desktop browser to address multiple vulnerabilities. The patches apply to Windows, Mac, and Linux versions, specifically targeting builds earlier than 154.0.8037.92 and 154.0.8037.93.
stories.why: Unpatched browser vulnerabilities are primary vectors for remote code execution and system compromise.
stories.action: Update Chrome to version 154.0.8037.92 or higher.

stories.title: Why CISOs Struggle to Answer the Board's Three Hardest Questions, and How to Fix the Report
stories.abstract: Security teams often struggle to provide clear, high-level answers to board members because they rely on fragmented data from disparate tools. This manual, spreadsheet-heavy reporting process fails to translate technical metrics into the business-centric insights that executives require for effective oversight.
stories.why: Poor communication between security teams and boards leads to misaligned risk management and insufficient budget allocation for critical security initiatives.

stories.title: [Control systems] CODESYS security advisory (AV26-983)
CISA Malcolm
ISC Stormcast For Friday, October 2nd, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10120, (Fri, Oct 2nd)
stories.abstract: The provided source material for the SANS ISC Stormcast dated October 2nd, 2026, is empty. Consequently, there is no information available to summarize regarding current security threats or technical developments.

stories.title: HPE security advisory (AV26-982)
stories.abstract: HPE has released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across several product lines, including Instant ON access points, Telco Service Orchestrator, various Compute Scale-up and Superdome Flex servers, and the Unified OSS Console.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in enterprise infrastructure and management consoles can lead to unauthorized access, privilege escalation, or remote code execution within critical environments.
stories.action: Review HPE security bulletins and update affected firmware and software to the specified versions.

stories.title: OpenSSL security advisory (AV26-980)
JetBrains security advisory (AV26-979)
stories.abstract: JetBrains has released security updates addressing vulnerabilities across several products, including Hub, IntelliJ IDEA, Rider, TeamCity, and YouTrack. Administrators should verify their current versions against the latest releases to ensure all identified security flaws are properly mitigated.
stories.why: Unpatched development and CI/CD tools are high-value targets for supply chain attacks and unauthorized access to source code environments.
stories.action: Update Hub, IntelliJ IDEA, Rider, TeamCity, and YouTrack to the latest patched versions.

stories.title: AI agents hacked the hackers, stealing email addresses from security research org
stories.abstract: Attackers exploited a chain of vulnerabilities in the Zammad helpdesk software to hijack sessions, execute arbitrary code, and gain root-level access to the underlying system.
stories.why: This exploit chain allows for complete system compromise, potentially exposing sensitive communications and internal security research data.
stories.action: Update Zammad to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: A Flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac App Could Have Let Hackers Grab Sensitive Data
stories.abstract: A security vulnerability in the ChatGPT desktop application for macOS, which could have allowed unauthorized access to sensitive user data, has been addressed by OpenAI. The flaw highlights the growing attack surface presented by AI-integrated software.
stories.why: AI applications often store sensitive session data or conversation history locally, making them high-value targets for credential theft or data exfiltration.
stories.action: Update the ChatGPT macOS application to the latest version.

stories.title: Dutch Police Arrest 24-Year-Old Amsterdam Man in ShinyHunters Investigation
stories.abstract: Dutch authorities apprehended a 24-year-old Amsterdam resident linked to the ShinyHunters cybercriminal syndicate. Beyond his alleged involvement in large-scale data theft and extortion, investigators discovered evidence on his devices indicating he was actively plotting the murder of two individuals.
stories.why: This arrest highlights the dangerous intersection of cybercrime and physical violence, marking a significant escalation in the threat profile of prolific hacking groups.

stories.title: SWIFT Banking & Government Middleware Enables RCE
stories.abstract: Middleware components utilized by government entities and SWIFT banking systems contain critical vulnerabilities. These flaws could allow attackers to achieve remote code execution, potentially bypassing hardware-based multi-factor authentication mechanisms in highly secure environments.
stories.why: Exploitation of these flaws could grant unauthorized access to sensitive financial and governmental infrastructure, undermining core authentication security controls.
stories.action: Apply available security patches for your middleware infrastructure immediately.

stories.title: Microsoft says threat actors are ahead in the early AI race
Two Zero-Days Exploited in Attack on Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure
stories.abstract: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure reported a cyberattack leveraging two zero-day vulnerabilities within the Zammad helpdesk software. The incident is notable for the attackers' use of agentic AI to facilitate the exploitation process.
stories.why: The integration of agentic AI in exploit chains signals a shift toward more autonomous, efficient, and scalable offensive operations.

stories.title: GitLab warns of critical RCE vulnerability in AI Gateway service
stories.abstract: GitLab has issued an urgent security advisory regarding a critical remote code execution vulnerability within its AI Gateway service. This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands on affected instances, potentially leading to full system compromise.
stories.why: Remote code execution in infrastructure components poses a severe risk of unauthorized access, data exfiltration, and lateral movement within internal networks.
stories.action: Update GitLab AI Gateway to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Alleged KillSec Ransomware Mastermind a 16-Year-Old
stories.abstract: International law enforcement agencies have dismantled the KillSec ransomware group, an operation responsible for approximately 500 global victimizations over the last two years. Authorities identified a 16-year-old individual as the primary architect behind the criminal enterprise.
stories.why: This highlights the ongoing trend of juvenile involvement in sophisticated ransomware operations and the efficacy of cross-border law enforcement cooperation.

stories.title: Android 17 Advanced Protection Locks Accessibility Services to Verified Accessibility Tools
ScreenConnect Client (Ab)used by Attackers, (Thu, Oct 1st)
stories.abstract: Attackers are increasingly leveraging legitimate remote management software like ScreenConnect to facilitate unauthorized access. By utilizing pre-installed or easily deployed administrative tools, threat actors can maintain persistence and execute commands while blending in with standard network traffic and administrative workflows.
stories.why: Living-off-the-land techniques using remote access tools bypass traditional signature-based detection, complicating incident response and visibility for security operations teams.

stories.title: In Other News: $15K iCloud Spoofing Bugs, AI Policy Experts Phished, Adblocker Spies on AI Chats
stories.abstract: SecurityWeek reports a collection of recent developments, including Kiteworks addressing over 100 vulnerabilities, the release of Microsoft's 2026 Digital Defense Report, and the discovery of two dozen security flaws in Android applications through AI-assisted analysis.
stories.why: These updates highlight ongoing risks in enterprise file transfer systems and mobile application security, alongside broader strategic shifts in the threat landscape.
stories.action: Update Kiteworks instances to the latest patched version.

stories.title: The EDR blind spot: 3 ways browser attacks evade endpoint telemetry
stories.abstract: Browser-based threats are increasingly bypassing traditional endpoint detection and response systems. By exploiting session tokens, malicious extensions, and user-level manipulation, these attacks operate within the browser environment, leaving few actionable traces for standard security tools to identify or block.
stories.why: Attackers are shifting focus to browser-native vectors that evade EDR visibility, necessitating a defense-in-depth approach focused on browser-level security controls.

stories.title: Custom malware used in Citrix 0-day attacks targeting govt, banks, professional services
stories.abstract: Threat actors are exploiting undisclosed Citrix vulnerabilities to deploy custom malware against government, financial, and professional service organizations. The campaign's origins remain unidentified, and questions persist regarding the delayed disclosure timeline from the vendor.
stories.why: Unpatched zero-day exploits targeting critical infrastructure and financial sectors pose significant risks of data exfiltration and persistent network compromise.
